transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
In Michigan, the race for the Senate has taken a new twist as a former Democratic primary hopeful
now says she's endorsing the Republican candidate.
And Piers Ava Berger has more.
Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens broke with her party Sunday.
She posted on her social media that she was endorsing Michigan's Republican candidate,
Mike Rogers, over fellow Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.
I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today.
I don't belong in Abdul's campaign.
Stevens also endorsed Rogers outside of a church event and said she's still a Democrat
but didn't feel welcome in El-Sayed's campaign.
The split comes after El-Sayed told reporters he didn't want Stevens to attend
a different church service Sunday with him that was meant to show unity among Democrats.
In August, El-Sayed beat Stevens in a bitter primary in which the pair clashed over U.S. support for Israel.
Initially, Stevens had endorsed El-Sayed in the tight race.
Ava Berger, NPR News, Washington.
The federal judge has thrown out the Trump administration's attempt to block the certification
of results from a key Senate race in Alaska if the Republican incumbent loses.
President Trump ordered the suit because two candidates have similar names.
In a ruling released today, U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason found the federal government
doesn't have the ability to bring this lawsuit.
The Justice Department is expected to appeal.
Democratic Senator Chris Murphy has suffered a stroke.
His office says he was hospitalized yesterday after experiencing numbness in his arm
when he was at his son's hockey game.
Doctors discovered he'd had a stroke and he was moved to Johns Hopkins Hospital for monitoring.
As doctors say, they're encouraged by the 53-year-old's progress. Murphy is a leading foreign policy voice in the Democratic Party.
President Trump hits the campaign trail in the Midwest today, campaigning on behalf of Republican candidates in Iowa and Kansas.
And here's Stephen Fowler-Hesmore.
The president is holding his final in-person rallies of the midterms.
In two states, he won decisively in 2024, but now have a lot of voters unhappy with his agenda.
His first stop, Dubuque, Iowa, in the second congressional district that Trump won by double digits,
but now is on the edge of the competitive map.
Then, Trump goes to Kansas, where polls show Republicans could take control of the governor's office
but lose the Senate race in another heavily conservative state.
Both parties are spending hundreds of millions of dollars in these last few days to get out the vote
with a larger-than-usual number of House and Senate races expected to be close.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News.
Andreas Amgren won today's New York City Marathon for the men, the Swede, running in his first race,
one in two hours, six minutes and one second, for the women, Sheila Chebkiru,
pulled away from two close competitors at the end, winning the race in two hours, 24 minutes and 36 seconds.
You're listening to NPR News.
India's capital, New Delhi, saw one of its largest demonstrations against the country's election commissioner.
A sense of thousands marched today to demand his resignation.
Protesters accused the election body of manipulating voter lists to favor India's ruling party.
And Piers Omkar Kandekar has more.
Supporters of India's opposition parties waved flags and beat drums
as they walked past hundreds of riot police in New Delhi.
They also chanted slogans.
Accusing election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of disenfranchising Indian citizens
after a controversial revision of India's voter lists dropped millions of names.
Such protests have been taking place across India for more than a month.
In his speech, opposition leader Rahul Gandhi announced plans
to take legal action against India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Modi had chaired the panel that appointed the election commissioner.
Omkar Kandekar, NPR News, New Delhi.
The federal judge has refused to dismiss a proposed class-action lawsuit against McDonald's
over its McRib sandwich.
The suit claims the fast-food giant defrauded customers
about the meat that's used in the sandwich,
saying it's actually a lower-quality pork product like shoulder, stomach, heart or tripe,
which means customers the suit says are being overcharged for the sandwich.
McDonald's says no reasonable customer would expect rib meat in a McRib sandwich.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers over Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race
Federal judge tosses Trump administration's suit to block certifying Alaska Senate results if Republican incumbent loses
Democratic Senator Chris Murphy hospitalized after suffering a stroke, now being monitored at Johns Hopkins
President Trump campaigns in Iowa and Kansas ahead of the midterm elections
Andreas Amgren wins men's New York City Marathon; Sheila Chebkiru takes women's title
Thousands march in New Delhi demanding resignation of election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over voter list revisions
Federal judge refuses to dismiss class-action lawsuit claiming McDonald's McRib contains lower-quality pork
